chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Sulayman ibn Salih, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:

For the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the 'alaqah forty dinars, for the mudghah sixty dinars, and for the bone eighty dinars. Then when it is clothed with flesh, it is one hundred dinars; then it remains one hundred dinars until it cries out at birth.
He said: “Then when it cries out at birth, the diyah is complete.”

key_terms.النُّطْفَةِ: the fertilized drop; the earliest stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْعَظْمِ: the stage at which bone has formed
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةِ: the clinging clot-like stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: the chewed-like lump stage of embryonic development
key_terms.كَامِلَةٌ: complete or full, meaning the full diyah becomes due
key_terms.كُسِيَ: was clothed or covered, referring here to being covered with flesh
key_terms.يَسْتَهِلَّ: to cry out at birth, indicating live birth

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a fetus at different stages of development in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states graded diyah amounts for the fetus at different stages of development, beginning from the nutfah and increasing through the stages until full liability applies after live birth. It is significant in fiqh because it defines legal compensation according to fetal development and distinguishes between prenatal loss and a child born alive.
